events.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

DATA_FILE=/tmp/smoke/books.json PORT=3999 node server.js & sleep 1
B=http://127.0.0.1:3999

ID=$(node -e "console.log(JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/tmp/smoke/books.json')).at(0).id)")

curl -s $B/books/$ID | sed -n '/<article>/,/<\/article>/p'
cat /tmp/smoke/books.json

events.content:
I've built the app. It's a small Node server with no dependencies that saves your books to `data/books.json`. The 11 automated tests pass, and I ran the real server with curl requests: adding a book, opening its page and marking it finished all worked, and the JSON file had the right contents. I haven't clicked through it in a browser or tried the "Copy link" button.

**To run it:**
```
npm start      # http://127.0.0.1:3000
npm test
```

**What it does:**
- **Home page:** shows "Currently reading" (each with a "Mark as finished" button), "Finished" (with the date you finished each one), and a form to add a book. Title is required; author and notes are optional.
- **Book page** (`/books/<id>`): shows the title, author, your notes, and when you started or finished it. The page address is the link you send someone, and there's a "Copy link" button for it. Each book gets a short random id, like `/books/o8ijrZqb`.
- **Saving:** books are still there after a restart. A crash halfway through saving can't leave a half-written file, and books added at the same moment aren't lost. If the file ever gets corrupted, the app refuses to start and tells you, rather than replacing your books with an empty list.

**Things to know:**
- **Who can open a shared link:** they can only open it if they can reach your computer. By default the app only listens on your own machine, so a link won't work for anyone else yet. Start it with `HOST=0.0.0.0` to make it reachable on your network, or put it on a server for people outside your network.
- **No accounts means no privacy:** anyone who can reach the app can see every book and add or finish books, not just the one you linked. I did block other websites from submitting the forms on your behalf.
- **Notes can only be written when you add a book.** There's no way to edit them, or a book, afterwards, and no way to delete a book, because you didn't ask for those. Editing notes is probably the first thing you'll want, and it would be a small addition.
- **Your book list isn't tracked by git.** I added `data/` to `.gitignore`. Remove that line if you want it in version control.
- **Settings:** `PORT`, `HOST` and `DATA_FILE` environment variables change the port, address and file location.

The code is in `server.js` (startup), `src/store.js` (saving to the JSON file), `src/app.js` (pages and form handling), `src/views.js` (the HTML) and `test/app.test.js`. Nothing is committed yet.
